content.text:
Fixed. The emphasis was being hidden from the em/strong scanner by the reference-link mask, which ran before the tokenizer ever decided to reject the link.

**Cause.** In `inlineTokens` in src/Lexer.ts, every reference link whose label resolves is masked out as `[aaaa...]` so delimiters inside a link do not pair with ones outside. That mask covered the whole of `[foo *bar [baz](/url) qux*][ref]`. The tokenizer later rejects the outer link because its text contains another link, re-scanning the text as plain prose. But the emphasis scanner reads the masked copy, where the asterisks were now letters, so it could never find them. Inline links were unaffected because their mask regex forbids nested brackets.

**Fix.**
- src/Lexer.ts: added a check used by the mask, which only masks a resolvable reference link when it will actually become a link token. It skips masking when the label contains an inline link or a resolvable reference link, since the tokenizer will reject it. Images are still always masked, and an inner image does not count as a link.
- src/rules.ts: pulled the existing inline-link search pattern into a shared rule so the lexer can run it over a label. The existing mask behaviour is unchanged.

**Tests.**
- CommonMark example 533 was marked as expected-to-fail in both the commonmark and gfm spec fixtures. It now passes, so I removed that marker.
- Added a unit test in test/unit/marked.test.js covering the bug report cases with `*`, `_`, `**`, an inner reference link, plus image cases that must still produce a link or image.
